key_insight: Neutron-irradiated CdS/CdTe solar cells show persistent performance losses after 18 months, with partial recovery under mild illuminated annealing but fill-factor degradation during prolonged treatment.
engineering_relevance: Radiation-tolerant CdTe space photovoltaics require coordinated optimization of substrate transparency, absorber stability, and contact recovery.
method: Irradiate cells in a 90 kW TRIGA reactor for 10–150 min at nominal neutron fluences of 3.3 × 10^14–5.0 × 10^15 n/cm².
Characterize electrical performance after 18 months of storage and optical transmission of co-irradiated FTO-coated glass.
Track device recovery during annealing at 70 °C under one-sun illumination.
evidence_signal: FTO-coated glass transmission at 500 nm fell from 80% to 50% after 60 min of irradiation; annealed cells reached their highest efficiency after 4 h, while longer treatment substantially degraded fill factor.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish the underlying defect mechanisms or whether reactor irradiation and delayed measurements predict performance in space.
paper_title: Persistent Neutron Irradiation Effects and Partial Recovery in Thin-Film CdS/CdTe Solar Cells
